items.title: Define degraded one-host fallback for unavailable second hosts
items.context: The execution plan should avoid blocking development when only one host can run. The fallback must not pretend to provide two-host independence; it should require an explicit reason, artifact marker, stronger local evidence, and clear limits for high-risk changes.
items.userSees: User sees: The execution plan now says 3x2 remains the default, but when a second host is unavailable or out of credits, Lattice may use a clearly marked 3-round x 1-host degraded fallback with reason codes and stronger evidence.

happy.desc: The document preserves 3x2 as the default and introduces 3x1 only as an explicitly degraded fallback for unavailable second hosts.
The document lists acceptable second-host unavailable reasons such as credit exhausted, auth missing, runtime unavailable, provider outage, and rate limited.

edge.desc: The document states degraded 3x1 is not equivalent to two-host independence and must be shown as a lower assurance level.
The document defines limits or extra approval expectations for high-risk or decision-doc changes using degraded review.

adversarial.desc: The document requires negative controls so the gate cannot silently downgrade or treat fabricated host unavailability as valid.
The document keeps degraded local review separate from Authority receipt completion and full 3x2 claims.

verificationEvidence.note: The document preserves full 3x2 as default and introduces 3x1 only as degraded single-host review.
